name: Lashi

allophone_rules.notes: Checked-syllable coda. The finals table writes the ⟨-b⟩ rimes voiceless — ⟨ab⟩ [ap], ⟨oeb⟩ [op] — so a ⟨b⟩ closing a syllable is [p], while ⟨by⟩ is the labial-plus-medial-glide onset [pj]/[bj] and keeps its onset value.
Word-final ⟨-b⟩ is the checked rime ⟨ab⟩ [ap] / ⟨oeb⟩ [op] of the finals table.

Checked-syllable coda: the finals table writes ⟨id⟩ [it] and ⟨ed⟩ [et]. Its ⟨aid⟩ [at] and ⟨oid⟩ [ot] rows also monophthongise the nucleus, which this spec does NOT follow — ⟨oi⟩ and ⟨ai⟩ keep their glides here, so ⟨anghoid⟩ is [ʔaŋojt] and not [ʔaŋot], because the Waingmaw transcriptions of that word back the glide. Only the coda consonant of those rows is encoded.
Word-final ⟨-d⟩ is the checked rime ⟨id⟩ [it] / ⟨ed⟩ [et] of the finals table.

Checked-syllable coda: the finals table writes ⟨ag⟩ [ak], ⟨ug⟩ [uk], ⟨eig⟩ [ək]. Only the coda consonant of those rows is encoded — the chart's ⟨oug⟩ [ok] also monophthongises the nucleus, where this spec keeps ⟨ou⟩ as [ow]. ⟨gy⟩ is the velar-plus-medial-glide onset [kj]/[ɡj] and keeps its onset value.
Word-final ⟨-g⟩ is the checked rime ⟨ag⟩ [ak] / ⟨ug⟩ [uk] of the finals table.

A syllable written with no initial consonant letter begins with [ʔ] — the alphabet chart lists the zero initial as [ʔ]. Word-initially `positional_graphemes` supplies it; word-internally the onset falls between two vowel letters, so the rule hangs the glottal on the preceding nucleus: ⟨Noa⟩ [nɔʔa], ⟨Midian⟩ [midiʔan]. The glottal-initial nuclei are listed alongside the bare ones because a word-initial slot has already been rewritten by `positional_graphemes` when this rule sees it, and a second zero-initial syllable can follow the first: ⟨ia⟩ is [ʔiʔa].

⟨o⟩ is [o] in a closed rime — ⟨oin⟩, ⟨oid⟩, ⟨oug⟩, ⟨oem⟩ are all written with [o] in the finals table — and [ɔ] in an open one, where the shipped Waingmaw transcriptions contrast ⟨lo⟩ [lɔ] with ⟨loo⟩ [lo] and ⟨mo⟩ [mɔ] with ⟨moo⟩ [mo]. The open/closed split is a Waingmaw observation, not a claim of the Cangmokhung chart, which merges ⟨o⟩ and ⟨oo⟩ as [o]; [o] stays in the lattice as the second candidate for ⟨o⟩. The ⟨ʼ⟩ exclusion follows the Waingmaw transcriptions against the chart, which gives ⟨oʼ⟩ as [oʔ] explicitly: the glottal final closes the rime orthographically but does not lower the nucleus there, so ⟨khoʼ⟩ is [kʰɔʔ].
The `lsi-o-closed-syllable` rule for a word-initial ⟨o⟩, whose slot `positional_graphemes` has already rewritten to the glottal-initial nucleus: ⟨og⟩ is [ʔok], not [ʔɔk].

ancestors.notes: Descent per Glottolog classification of Lashi (lash1243).

notes: Lashi (Lacid, Leqi) is a Burmish (Sino-Tibetan) language of Myanmar and Yunnan written in a Latin orthography devised in the 1970s. The letter values follow the published alphabet chart for the Cangmokhung standard: three obstruent series (plain ⟨b d g z j⟩, glottalised ⟨p t k zh jh⟩, aspirated ⟨ph th kh x c⟩), a postposed ⟨h⟩ marking the glottalised sonorants ⟨mh nh nyh ngh rh lh yh⟩, and a finals table giving the rimes. A syllable written without an initial consonant letter begins with [ʔ], which the chart states explicitly and which `positional_graphemes` supplies word-initially. The checked rimes ⟨-b -d -g⟩ are [p t k]: the allophone rules turn a syllable-closing voiced-stop letter into its voiceless counterpart, excluding ⟨by gy⟩ and friends where the following ⟨y⟩ makes the stop an onset with a medial glide. ⟨ʼ⟩ is the glottal final of ⟨aʼ⟩ [aʔ], ⟨oʼ⟩ [oʔ], ⟨uʼ⟩ [uʔ]. Where the descriptive traditions disagree the spec ranks the Waingmaw values first and keeps the Cangmokhung chart values as second candidates in the lattice: the obstruent letters ⟨b d g z j⟩ are read voiced ([b d ɡ d͡z d͡ʑ]) rather than voiceless, ⟨sh⟩ is [ɕ] rather than [ʃ], ⟨r⟩ is [ɹ] rather than [r], and ⟨ei⟩/⟨eu⟩ is [ɨ] rather than [ə]. ⟨oi ai ou au⟩ carry no such alternative and are single-valued [oj aj aw ow]: the chart monophthongises them only in its closed rimes ⟨oid⟩ [ot], ⟨aid⟩ [at], ⟨oug⟩ [ok], a coda-conditioned alternation this spec does not encode, because the Waingmaw transcriptions of ⟨anghoid⟩ and ⟨mougmyid⟩ back the glide in exactly that position. ⟨q⟩ appears in the shipped Wiktionary-derived gold, in ⟨qei⟩ [ɣɨ], and in no alphabet chart; one gold word is not evidence for a letter value, so it is deliberately left unmapped and needs a native check. Lexical tone is written — ⟨:⟩ low, ⟨”⟩ high, ⟨ʼ⟩ high-falling, unmarked falling — but the tone letters are not emitted, because the height of an unmarked syllable is a lexical fact this description does not carry, so an elevated PER floor against tone-bearing narrow gold is expected and documented. Creaky phonation, which the chart's apostrophe notation places on the vowel after a glottalised consonant, is likewise left unencoded, as is the fronting of ⟨a⟩ to [æ] before a labial coda that the Waingmaw transcriptions show. Stress is not separately contrastive (documented exemption).

sources.notes: Consulted. Tertiary alphabet chart for the 1970s Latin orthography, given for the Cangmokhung dialect: initials with their IPA (including the zero initial as [ʔ] and the glottalised sonorant digraphs), a finals table with the checked rimes ⟨ab⟩ [ap], ⟨id⟩ [it], ⟨ag⟩ [ak], ⟨ug⟩ [uk], ⟨oug⟩ [ok], ⟨eig⟩ [ək], ⟨aʼ⟩ [aʔ], ⟨oʼ⟩ [oʔ], ⟨uʼ⟩ [uʔ], and the tone marks ⟨:⟩ low, ⟨”⟩ high, ⟨ʼ⟩ high-falling with unmarked falling. The primary source of the letter values encoded here.
